name: mpc74xx_l2_enable
prose: Precondition: runs on an MPC74xx-class CPU with access to SPR_L2CR; l2cr_config is the desired L2CR value. Postcondition: it chooses the in-progress bit to wait on from the processor version (L2CR_L2IP for MPC7400 and MPC7410, L2CR_L2I otherwise). If the current L2CR value already has L2CR_L2E set, it returns that current L2CR value and writes nothing. Otherwise it writes (l2cr_config with L2CR_L2E cleared) ORed with L2CR_L2I to L2CR to start an invalidate, spins until the chosen in-progress bit reads as clear (a hardware condition that this function cannot itself guarantee), issues powerpc_sync, writes l2cr_config to L2CR, issues powerpc_sync and returns l2cr_config. The L2 is therefore enabled by the final write only if l2cr_config itself has L2CR_L2E set; the function does not set that bit.
note: Read mp_cpudep.c:141-172. Reviewers right: round 1 (the code returns l2cr_config without forcing L2E), round 2/15 (contract weaker than prose; the early return leaves SPRs unchanged). Contract left empty: the function reads and writes SPRs. Slice cut the head.

name: DB_SHOW_COMMAND(tlb0, tlb0_print_tlbentries)
prose: Generated function (debugger command "show tlb0", defined with DB_SHOW_COMMAND(tlb0, tlb0_print_tlbentries)). Precondition: called from the kernel debugger on a Book-E PowerPC CPU where the MAS registers and tlbre can be used. Postcondition: prints "TLB0 entries:" and then, for each way from 0 to TLB0_WAYS-1 and each entry index from 0 to TLB0_ENTRIES_PER_WAY-1, writes MAS0 (TLB select 0 and the way) and MAS2 (the entry index), executes isync and tlbre, reads MAS1, MAS2, MAS3 and MAS7, computes the table index with tlb0_tableidx(mas2, way) and calls tlb_print_entry with it and those registers. It returns nothing and changes MAS0 and MAS2 as a side effect.
note: Read booke/pmap.c:3067-3096. The slice 3083-3126 holds the tail of this command and the whole tlb1 command (3101-3125); the packet i=0 prose describes the tlb0 command, so it is fixed under the macro invocation head (the generated function name is the macro expansion; arguments not verified against DB_SHOW_COMMAND).

name: fpu_execute
prose: Precondition: tf is the trap frame of the faulting thread, fe is an FP emulator state whose fe_fpstate points to the thread's FPU state, insn points to the instruction word to emulate. Postcondition: it first copies the FPSCR word from fe_fpstate into fe_fpscr. For load/store opcodes (the D-form lfs..stfdu range and the X-form opcode 31 forms) the effective address is computed from tf->fixreg; stfiwx stores a word with copyout; the other X-form opcode-31 forms must be recognized FP load/store ones or it returns NOTFPU; an update form with RA = 0 returns NOTFPU. A store copies out with copyout (single precision values are converted first), a load copies in with copyin into the FP register (single precision values converted to double); a faulting copyin or copyout returns FAULT; on success an update form writes the address back to tf->fixreg[ra] and 0 is returned immediately, without the FPSCR write-back below. For opcode 59 and 63 FP instructions the function decodes the operation (compare, round, convert to integer, FPSCR moves, negate, abs, move, select, add, subtract, multiply, divide, sqrt, reciprocal estimates, fused multiply forms), writes results or FPSCR/CR fields as the instruction requires, and returns NOTFPU for an unrecognized extended opcode; any other primary opcode returns NOTFPU. After a recognized FP instruction the result (if any) is imploded into the destination FP register, the FPSCR exception bits in fe_cx are merged into the new FPSCR value (FX, FEX, FPRF, VX), CR1 or the selected CR field is updated when the instruction asks for it, the new FPSCR word is stored into fe_fpstate, and the function returns FPE when the FEX bit is set in it and 0 otherwise.
note: Slice cut the head: real function fpu_execute (fpu_emu.c:259-786), read in full (2 DPRINTF-only and comment lines skipped). Reviewers right: round 1 (NOTFPU for update load/store with RA=0, 375-376); round 15 (not all successful emulations write FP registers and FPSCR: loads/stores return before 741-785, and several FPSCR/CR instructions write other state). The prior prose also missed the FPE return (783-784).

name: fpu_sqrt
prose: Precondition: fe is an FP emulator state whose first operand fe_f1 holds an exploded (unpacked) floating-point number. Postcondition: returns a pointer to the result number. For a NaN operand it sets FPSCR_VXSNAN in fe->fe_cx and returns &fe->fe_f1 unchanged; for a zero operand it sets FPSCR_ZX in fe_cx, changes the operand's class to infinity and returns it; for a negative operand it sets FPSCR_VXSQRT and returns the pointer from fpu_newnan(fe); for an infinity it returns &fe->fe_f1 unchanged. Otherwise it halves the exponent (doubling the mantissa first when the exponent is odd), computes the square root of the 4-word mantissa one bit at a time into fp_mant[0..3] of fe_f1, sets fp_sticky to the OR of the remaining remainder words, and returns &fe->fe_f1. It takes no locks and modifies only *fe (the operand, fe_cx).
note: Slice cut the head and tail: real function fpu_sqrt(struct fpemu *fe) (fpu_sqrt.c:187-411), read lines 187-345 and 395-411 (the middle bit-loop for words 2 and 3, 346-394, is the same pattern and was not read line by line). No fp_sqrt exists in the file; the old prose assumed an x argument pre-normalized by the caller, which is wrong: normalization happens inside (255-263).

name: ATOMIC_STORE_LOAD(long)
prose: Generated function atomic_load_acq_long, produced by the macro invocation ATOMIC_STORE_LOAD(long) in the powerpc64 build (the macro is defined at atomic.h:503-520, invoked at 528). Precondition: p points to a readable, suitably aligned u_long. Postcondition: it reads the whole u_long *p into a local, then executes powerpc_lwsync(), and returns the value read. It takes no lock and has no error return. On 32-bit powerpc the same name is instead a separate inline function (atomic.h:536-541) that returns atomic_load_acq_int of the pointer cast to u_int, widened to u_long.
note: Read atomic.h:503-553. Reviewers right (rounds 15 and 17): the 64-bit macro version does a plain full-width u_long load followed by lwsync (509-511); the cast-to-u_int wrapper is the 32-bit variant. The slice holds only the macro, so the macro invocation is used as the name.

name: ATOMIC_STORE_LOAD(long)
prose: Generated function atomic_store_rel_long, produced by the macro invocation ATOMIC_STORE_LOAD(long) in the powerpc64 build (macro at atomic.h:503-520). Precondition: p points to a writable, suitably aligned u_long. Postcondition: it executes powerpc_lwsync() and then stores the whole u_long v to *p (the store statement is on the stripped line 519 of the macro, read from the macro's shape). It returns nothing, takes no lock, and has no error return. On 32-bit powerpc the same name is a separate inline function (atomic.h:543-548) that calls atomic_store_rel_int with the pointer cast to u_int and the value truncated to u_int.
note: Read atomic.h:514-520 and 543-548; line 519 (the store itself) was a blank/comment-stripped line in my dump, so the full-width store is taken from the reviewers (rounds 15, 17) and the macro pattern, not verified line by line.

name: pmac_therm_manage_fans
prose: Precondition: the global sensors and fans lists are well-formed with valid read and set callbacks. Postcondition: returns nothing. If enable_pmac_thermal is zero it returns at once without touching any sensor or fan. Otherwise, for each sensor it calls the read callback and replaces last_val with the result only when it is positive (otherwise the previous last_val is kept); if last_val exceeds the sensor's max_temp it increments critical_count, prints a warning and, when critical_count reaches MAX_CRITICAL_COUNT, prints a message and calls shutdown_nice(RB_POWEROFF); otherwise it decrements critical_count when it is above zero. Then for each fan it computes for every sensor the excess of the (max_temp-capped) temperature over target_temp as a percentage, clamped at 0, tracking the sum over all sensors and the maximum over sensors in the fan's zone; with no sensors the fan's set callback is called with default_rpm and the fan is skipped; otherwise the zone maximum (or the average when the zone has no sensor), capped at 100, is converted to a speed between min_rpm and max_rpm; when that speed is at least the fan's last_val the speed is adopted and the hysteresis timer reset, otherwise the timer is decremented and the speed adopted only when the timer reaches 0; finally the fan's set callback is called with fan->last_val.
note: Read powermac_thermal.c:96-202. Reviewers right: round 1 (early return when enable_pmac_thermal is false, 105-106); round 15 (the fan speed is adopted when it is >= last_val, 190-192, otherwise only after the timer expires; the earlier prose had this reversed).

name: opalpci_read_config
prose: Precondition: dev is a valid opalpci device whose softc holds phb_id; bus, slot, func, reg and width describe the configuration access. Postcondition: the configuration address is built from bus, slot and func. For width 1, 2 or 4 it calls OPAL to read that many bytes, converting widths 2 and 4 from big-endian to host order (the width-1 byte is returned as is); for any other width no OPAL read is made, the value becomes 0xffffffff and width is treated as 4. If the OPAL call returned an error, or the value equals the all-ones mask for the width (0xff, 0xffff or 0xffffffff), and the error is not OPAL_HARDWARE, it queries the EEH freeze status of the default PE and clears the freeze (OPAL_EEH_ACTION_CLEAR_FREEZE_ALL) when the status is not OPAL_EEH_STOPPED_NOT_FROZEN. If the OPAL call returned an error the result is 0xffffffff (for every width); otherwise the result is the value read, so an all-ones read of width 1 or 2 is returned as 0xff or 0xffff, not 0xffffffff, while an unsupported width returns 0xffffffff (after the same EEH check).
note: Slice cut the head; real function opalpci_read_config (opal_pci.c:499-558), read in full. Reviewer round 15 right: width-1/2 all-ones reads give 0xff/0xffff (word is not overwritten unless error != OPAL_SUCCESS, 553-554). Also unsupported widths run the EEH check because word equals the 4-byte mask (531-542).

name: native_bs_rs_8
prose: Precondition: bsh plus ofs denotes a mapped, readable 8-byte device location. Postcondition: it computes the address with __ppc_ba(bsh, ofs), reads the 64-bit value from that volatile address, executes powerpc_iomb() (an I/O memory barrier) and returns the value. Unlike native_bs_rs_1, _2 and _4 it does not emit a KTR trace. It takes no locks and allocates nothing.
note: Read bus_machdep.c:225-235. Reviewers right: rounds 2 and 15 (the code calls powerpc_iomb() at 233); round 1 (claimed no powerpc_iomb) is wrong. The old prose claiming no barrier was also wrong.

name: REMAP(copyinstr)
prose: Generated-name function copyinstr, defined with the REMAP(copyinstr) wrapper. Precondition: udaddr is a user-space address of the current process, kaddr a kernel buffer of at least len bytes, len a byte count, done NULL or a writable size_t. Postcondition: it installs a fault handler (pcb_onfault) and copies the string byte by byte, mapping the user range in chunks with pmap_map_user_ptr. The result starts as ENAMETOOLONG: it returns 0 as soon as a NUL byte has been copied (that NUL is counted as transferred); it returns EFAULT if a mapping call fails or a fault occurs during the copy (the count is the bytes copied so far); and it returns ENAMETOOLONG when len bytes were copied without a NUL, which includes len == 0 (nothing is copied and no other error value is used for it). The fault handler is cleared before returning, and when done is non-NULL *done is set to the number of bytes counted as transferred in every case.
note: Read copyinout.c:236-287 (head 236-253 and the loop 253-287). Reviewer round 15 is wrong for this source: there is no EINVAL for len == 0; the initial value ENAMETOOLONG is returned with *done = 0 (250-251, 262, 282-286). Name is the REMAP macro wrapper plus the real function copyinstr.

name: powerpc_get_irq
prose: Precondition: node is a device-tree node handle (0 means none), pin an interrupt pin number. Postcondition: when node is 0 it returns pin immediately, without taking the lock. Otherwise it takes intr_table_lock and looks through piclist: if a PIC with that node already exists (real or earlier fake) it releases the lock and returns that PIC's base plus pin. If none matches it writes a new fake PIC entry at piclist[npics] (no device, the node, 124 irqs, 4 ipis, base = nirqs), adds 1 << 25 to nirqs, increments npics, then asserts npics < MAX_PICS (a KASSERT, checked after the entry was written and counted, so the write itself is not guarded), releases the lock and returns the new base plus pin. Sums are u_int arithmetic and may wrap.
note: Read intr_machdep.c:406-441. Reviewers right: round 2 (the KASSERT is after npics++, 433-436), round 15 (an existing fake PIC entry is matched by node at 415-417 and reused). Contract left empty (touches global piclist state).

name: csr_read
note: Not a function: csr_read is a statement-expression macro (riscvreg.h:261-265) that only runs a csrr instruction.

name: csr_read64
note: Not a function: csr_read64 is a macro (riscvreg.h:267-284); the 32-bit variant is a statement-expression retry loop around csrr instructions and the 64-bit variant just casts csr_read. It only computes a value.

name: bounce_bus_dmamap_create
prose: Precondition: dmat is an initialized bus_dma tag and mapp points to a writable bus_dmamap_t variable. Postcondition: if the tag's segment array is NULL it allocates it (M_NOWAIT) and returns ENOMEM if that fails. It then allocates a new map into *mapp and returns ENOMEM when that fails (*mapp is NULL in that case). If the tag could bounce (BF_COULD_BOUNCE) it creates the tag's bounce zone when missing (on failure it frees the new map and returns that error, leaving *mapp pointing at the freed map), sets DMAMAP_COULD_BOUNCE on the map, and, when BF_MIN_ALLOC_COMP is not yet set or the zone has maps and fewer than the maximum bounce pages, computes a page count and calls alloc_bounce_pages: a short allocation sets error to ENOMEM, which is kept when the minimum allocation had not yet completed (BF_MIN_ALLOC_COMP is set only if that first attempt succeeded) and cleared to 0 otherwise; bz->map_count is incremented in any case. If error is 0, dmat->map_count is incremented and 0 is returned with *mapp being the new map; on a nonzero error the new map is freed (*mapp left dangling) and the error returned.
note: Slice cut the head; real function bounce_bus_dmamap_create (busdma_bounce.c:242-318), read in full (line 260, the map allocation, was a comment-adjacent line not displayed but implied by 261-264). Reviewers: round 15 is mixed: the segments array allocation (249-258) is in this function, so the first complaint is wrong; the second is right for the map allocation failure (*mapp NULL) but *mapp is left dangling on the later failures (276, 314).

name: parse_metadata
prose: Precondition: early boot, with preload metadata reachable through preload_kmdp after preload_initkmdp(true); the ENVP, DDB symbol and FDT records may be absent. Postcondition: it calls preload_initkmdp(true) and sched_instance_select, sets boothowto from MODINFOMD_HOWTO, reads the kernel end address from MODINFOMD_KERNEND (the value it returns), and fetches the environment pointer: a non-NULL one initializes the static kernel environment from it, otherwise from the built-in static_kenv buffer. With DDB it fetches the symbol table bounds and registers them with db_fetch_ksymtab. With FDT it calls try_load_dtb and, when no environment pointer was supplied, parses the FDT bootargs into boothowto. It then calls parse_boot_hartid, which takes the boot hart from the MODINFOMD_BOOT_HARTID metadata when present and below UINT32_MAX, else from /chosen boot-hartid (FDT builds), panics if the boot hart is still invalid, and sets the per-CPU hart. It returns lastaddr.
note: Slice cut the head; real function parse_metadata (machdep.c:472-506) plus parse_boot_hartid (420-456), read in full. The MD_FETCH macro behavior when a record is missing was not read. Reviewers (rounds 1, 2, 15) complained about contract wording and the precondition on preload_kmdp: the code initializes it itself (481).

name: pmap_promote_l2
prose: Precondition: the pmap lock is held (asserted), l2 points to the pmap's level-2 entry for va whose page-table page has been filled, ml3 is the page-table page or NULL, lockp is the caller's PV lock slot. Postcondition: returns false at once when superpages are not enabled for the pmap. The L2 entry must have none of the PTE_RWX bits set (asserted; its valid bit is not checked here, the function dereferences the page it points to). It returns false, counting pmap_l2_p_failures, when the physical address of the first L3 entry is not 2MB-aligned, when any other L3 entry (scanned from the last to the second) does not map the expected consecutive physical page, when its promotion attributes differ from the first entry's, or when pmap_insert_pt_page fails for the page-table page. During the scan the write bit is cleared with an atomic compare-and-set on entries that are writable and not yet dirty, so a failure can leave some L3 entries with PTE_W cleared. On success the accessed bit of the new entry is kept only if it was set in every L3 entry, the page-table page is recorded, PV entries are promoted with pmap_pv_promote_l2 when the mapping is managed, the new superpage entry is stored in *l2, pmap_l2_promotions is incremented and true is returned. On every false return *l2 is unchanged.
note: Read pmap.c:3128-3239 in full. Reviewer round 15 right: the physical address of the first L3 entry must be L2-aligned, otherwise failure (3149-3154). Round 1 (the L2 entry must be a valid page-table entry): the code only asserts the RWX bits are clear (3138); validity is assumed from the caller. Slice cut the head.

name: do_trap_user
prose: Precondition: frame is the current thread's trap frame and the trap came from user mode with SPP and SIE clear in sstatus and SUM clear (all asserted with KASSERT). Postcondition: returns nothing. If scause has the interrupt bit set it calls intr_irq_handler(frame, INTR_ROOT_IRQ) and returns without calling intr_enable. Otherwise it calls intr_enable and dispatches on the exception code: access faults give SIGBUS (BUS_ADRERR) and misalignment SIGBUS (BUS_ADRALN) through call_trapsignal followed by userret; page faults go to page_fault_handler(frame, 1); a user ecall advances sepc by 4 and calls ecall_handler; an illegal instruction from a thread whose FP state has not been started clears the FP state, marks sstatus FS clean and sets PCB_FP_STARTED (lazy FPU enable) and otherwise delivers SIGILL (ILL_ILLTRP) and calls userret; a breakpoint delivers SIGTRAP (TRAP_BRKPT) and userret; any other exception dumps the registers and panics.
note: Slice cut the head; real function do_trap_user (trap.c:380-460), read in full. Reviewers right: round 1 (the SUM-clear KASSERT, 396-397, and the interrupt/page-fault success paths), round 15 (the interrupt path returns at 403 before intr_enable at 405, so interrupts are not enabled on every path).

name: jh7110_gpio_pin_setflags
prose: Precondition: dev is a JH7110 GPIO device, pin and flags are arbitrary uint32_t values. Postcondition: returns EINVAL without taking the lock or touching any register when pin >= GPIO_PINS. Otherwise, holding the driver mutex: when GPIO_PIN_INPUT is set it sets PAD_INPUT_EN and PAD_HYST in the pad register IOMUX_SYSCFG_288 + PAD_OFFSET(pin); it always clears the ENABLE_MASK field at the pin's position in the GP0_DOEN_CFG register (whatever flags say) and, when GPIO_PIN_INPUT is set, then sets DIROUT_DISABLE in that field; when GPIO_PIN_OUTPUT is set it clears the same ENABLE_MASK-wide field in GP0_DOUT_CFG and sets its low bit to 1, and clears PAD_INPUT_EN, PAD_PULLUP, PAD_PULLDOWN and PAD_HYST in the pad register. It releases the mutex and returns 0.
note: Slice cut the head; real function jh7110_gpio_pin_setflags (jh7110_gpio.c:215-256), read in full. Reviewer round 15 right: the DOUT_CFG field cleared is ENABLE_MASK wide, not 7 bits (244). The DOEN_CFG clear at 236 is unconditional. Did not read the GPIO_* macro definitions.

name: clnt_dg_call
prose: Precondition: cl is a datagram RPC client handle whose socket has the clnt_dg upcall installed (cu_socket->so_rcv.sb_upcallarg is the cu_socket state), ext is NULL or a callextra, args is the argument mbuf chain (NULL allowed for an async call), utimeout is the caller's timeout. Postcondition: returns an enum clnt_stat. If the client is closing or closed it returns RPC_CANTSEND immediately (the lock released, the request freed, nothing stored in the error structure). Otherwise it counts itself in cu_threads, selects the error structure (ext->rc_err, else cu->cu_error), connects the socket on first use (RPC_CANTSEND with errno on failure), and loops: encodes the call header, procedure and AUTH_MARSHALLed arguments (RPC_CANTENCODEARGS sets only re_status), waits for congestion window space (RPC_INTR for EINTR/ERESTART or RPC_CANTSEND for other msleep errors), queues a request record and sends the datagram with sosend (RPC_CANTSEND on send error), then waits for the reply for the retransmit interval: a request-record error gives RPC_CANTRECV with that errno, a timeout of 0 gives RPC_TIMEDOUT, an interrupted or failed wait gives RPC_INTR or RPC_CANTRECV, total time over the timeout gives RPC_TIMEDOUT with errno EWOULDBLOCK, and at each retransmit time the congestion window is halved, the feedback callback is called, and the request is sent again with an increased backoff (RPC_CANTRECV with ESHUTDOWN if the client closed meanwhile). On a reply it updates the round-trip estimates, decodes it with xdr_replymsg (RPC_CANTDECODERES on failure), and for an accepted SUCCESS reply validates the verifier with AUTH_VALIDATE, giving RPC_SUCCESS or RPC_AUTHERROR (a retransmitted RPCSEC_GSS call with an invalid verifier waits again instead); other replies go through _seterr_reply (which stores its details in cu->cu_error) and an authentication error triggers up to two credential refreshes and a repeat of the call with a new xid. On any exit through the out label it frees an unsent request mbuf and an unused reply chain, decrements cu_threads (waking the closer if closing), releases the lock, calls AUTH_VALIDATE(auth, xid, NULL, NULL) when the status is not RPC_SUCCESS, frees the request record and returns the status. The cs_lock is not held on return.
note: Slice cut the head; real function clnt_dg_call (clnt_dg.c:320-783), read in full (comment lines skipped; the line that hands the decoded results back at 735-736 was not displayed, and AUTH_REFRESH/GSS retry at 708-733 was read only as control flow). Reviewers right: round 1 (early errors have no pending entry; results come back through the results argument, not cr_mrep), round 15 (RPC_CANTENCODEARGS sets only re_status, 443, and CANTDECODERES likewise, 758).

name: clnt_dg_control
prose: Precondition: cl is a datagram client, request is a CLSET_/CLGET_ opcode and info points to storage of the type the request needs (it may be NULL only for CLSET_FD_CLOSE and CLSET_FD_NCLOSE). Postcondition: it takes the socket's cs_lock and releases it before every return. CLSET_FD_CLOSE and CLSET_FD_NCLOSE set cu_closeit to TRUE or FALSE and return TRUE even with a NULL info. For any other request a NULL info returns FALSE. CLSET_TIMEOUT and CLSET_RETRY_TIMEOUT return FALSE when time_not_ok rejects the timeval, otherwise store it in cu_total or cu_wait; CLGET_TIMEOUT and CLGET_RETRY_TIMEOUT copy those fields out; CLGET_SVC_ADDR copies the server address out and CLSET_SVC_ADDR copies a new one in; CLGET_XID reads, and CLSET_XID writes (as *info minus 1), the global rpc_xid, not a per-client field; CLGET_VERS, CLSET_VERS, CLGET_PROG and CLSET_PROG read or write the version and program words of the saved call header in network order; CLSET_ASYNC, CLSET_CONNECT, CLSET_WAITCHAN and CLSET_INTERRUPTIBLE set the matching cu fields (the last one sets cu_waitflag to PCATCH or 0) and CLGET_WAITCHAN and CLGET_INTERRUPTIBLE read them back; any other request returns FALSE. All the successful operations return TRUE.
note: Slice cut the head; real function clnt_dg_control (clnt_dg.c:812-942), read in full except a few single-line copies (lines 846, 856, 870, 922, 932, 934 were comment-stripped in my dump and are described from their case labels). Reviewers right: round 1 (NULL info still returns TRUE for FD_CLOSE/FD_NCLOSE, and the XID operations use the global rpc_xid), round 15 (CLSET_XID stores *info - 1, 876).

name: clnt_reconnect_connect
prose: Precondition: cl is a reconnect CLIENT whose cl_private is an initialized rc_data. Postcondition: returns an enum clnt_stat. Under rc_lock it waits while another thread is connecting (rc_connecting), returning RPC_INTR if the wait is interrupted (it changes no flag then), returns RPC_CANTSEND if the client is closed (even when rc_client is set), and returns RPC_SUCCESS if rc_client is already set. Otherwise it sets rc_connecting, switches the thread credentials to rc_ucred, and creates a socket (RPC_TLIERROR in rpc_createerr if that fails), optionally binds a reserved port, and creates a datagram client for connectionless transports, or for others sets SO_SNDTIMEO when a positive timeout is configured (RPC_CANTSEND with the errno if that fails) and creates a stream client; with TLS configured it runs rpctls_connect and on failure sets the status to the returned status or RPC_FAILED, closes and releases the new client. If no client was created it closes the socket, copies rpc_createerr's error into rc_err and returns rpc_createerr.cf_stat (which may be any status left by clnt_dg_create or clnt_vc_create). On success it configures the new client (connect mode, timeouts, wait channel, interruptibility, backchannel) and the status is RPC_SUCCESS. At the common exit it takes rc_lock again, stores newclient in rc_client unless the client was closed meanwhile (in which case the new client is closed and released and the returned status is still the one computed, possibly RPC_SUCCESS), clears rc_connecting, wakes waiters and returns the status.
note: Slice cut the head; real function clnt_reconnect_connect (clnt_rc.c:126-277), read in full. Reviewers right: round 1 (statuses can be any rpc_createerr.cf_stat), round 15 (the RPC_INTR return at 144 does not touch rc_connecting; and with rc_closed set the early return at 147-149 does not look at rc_client, while the exit at 257-260 can leave rc_client NULL after a successful connect).

name: clnt_vc_close
prose: Precondition: cl is a stream RPC client with a valid ct_data and the caller does not hold ct->ct_lock. Postcondition: returns nothing. If the client is already closed it returns at once without further effect; if it is closing it waits until closing ends and returns (neither early path wakes anyone). Otherwise, when ct_socket is non-NULL it sets ct_closing, clears the socket's receive upcall (and calls clnt_vc_upcallsdone) if one is installed, marks every pending request with xid 0 and error ESHUTDOWN and wakes it, and waits until ct_threads reaches zero; when ct_socket is NULL none of that is done. In the non-early path it then sets ct_closing to FALSE and ct_closed to TRUE, wakes sleepers on ct_tlsstate and on ct, and releases ct_lock. The socket itself is not closed here (that is done by clnt_vc_destroy).
note: Slice cut the head; real function clnt_vc_close (clnt_vc.c:799-850), read in full. Reviewers right: round 1 (pending-request abort and the ct_threads wait only occur when ct_socket is non-NULL, 819-843); round 15 (the early-return paths at 806-816 do not wake sleepers on ct or ct_tlsstate).

name: rpc_gss_init
prose: Precondition: auth is an RPCSEC_GSS handle whose private data gd is protected by gd_lock, options_ret points to writable result storage, and the vnet is set (asserted). Postcondition: under gd_lock it waits until gd_state is RPCSEC_GSS_START or RPCSEC_GSS_ESTABLISHED; if it is ESTABLISHED it releases the lock and returns TRUE without writing options_ret. Otherwise it sets the state to RPCSEC_GSS_CONTEXT and starts a new context negotiation: gc_proc becomes RPCSEC_GSS_INIT and gc_seq 0, a client credential is acquired from gd_clntprincipal for Kerberos when configured (a failure records the GSS status in options_ret and goes to the failure exit), the service principal name is imported (same failure handling), and the function loops calling gss_init_sec_context (the lucid variant for MIT Kerberos) with the thread credentials temporarily set to gd_ucred. A failing GSS status other than COMPLETE or CONTINUE_NEEDED, a failing RPC (CLNT_CALL_EXT of NULLPROC with the token), a server reply whose major status is neither COMPLETE nor CONTINUE_NEEDED, or a failed verification of the server's window MIC ends the loop with the GSS status stored in options_ret (a verify failure with an expired context also destroys the context and sets an RPC_GSS_ER_SYSTEMERROR/EPERM error). The server's handle and token replace the previous ones between rounds and gc_proc becomes CONTINUE_INIT. On GSS_S_COMPLETE with a verified window, options_ret receives the status, version and context, gc_proc becomes RPCSEC_GSS_DATA, gd_seq 1 and gd_win the server's window. At the out label, if gc_proc is not RPCSEC_GSS_DATA, rpc_createerr.cf_stat is set to RPC_AUTHERROR, a GSS error is recorded, any context is deleted, gd_state returns to RPCSEC_GSS_START, waiters are woken and FALSE is returned; otherwise gd_state becomes RPCSEC_GSS_ESTABLISHED, waiters are woken and TRUE is returned.
note: Slice cut the head: lines 770-1021 are inside rpc_gss_init (rpcsec_gss.c:754-1055; its debug message says rpc_gss_refresh); the real rpc_gss_refresh is at 1058-1092 and is outside the slice. Read rpc_gss_init 754-1055 in full except the middle of the context-initialization call. Reviewers right: round 1 (the early ESTABLISHED return does not write options_ret, 786-789); round 15 (the slice is GSS context establishment, not MSG_DENIED handling).

name: svc_rpc_gss_accept_sec_context
prose: Precondition: client is a client record (cl_sname may be NULL), rqst a request whose argument decodes as a gss_buffer_desc, gr and gc writable. Postcondition: the function first determines the Kerberos implementation (once) and, for MIT, presets the credential uid/gid to 65534. If svc_getargs of the token fails it sets cl_state to CLIENT_STALE and returns FALSE before taking any lock. Otherwise it takes svc_rpc_gss_lock exclusively around the accept call only: with no cl_sname it finds the server name matching rqst->rq_prog and rq_vers, runs gss_accept_sec_context (retrying after rpc_gss_acquire_svc_cred when the credentials expired and could be reacquired) and records the matching name in cl_sname, or, when no server name matches, frees the token, releases the lock and returns FALSE without changing cl_state; with an existing cl_sname it accepts with that name's credentials. It releases the lock and frees the token. If the GSS result in gr is neither GSS_S_COMPLETE nor CONTINUE_NEEDED it logs, sets cl_state to CLIENT_STALE and returns TRUE (the caller reads gr). Otherwise it fills gr's handle and window and the client's mechanism and qop; for GSS_S_COMPLETE it sets the credential expiration (capped by svc_rpc_gss_lifetime_max, 24 hours when indefinite), then for non-MIT exports the client name with gss_export_name and returns FALSE if that fails (the cl_cname name is left unreleased on that path), builds the raw credentials and ucred, sets the flavor and releases cl_cname. The function returns TRUE after that, or TRUE for CONTINUE_NEEDED.
note: Slice cut the head; real function svc_rpc_gss_accept_sec_context (svc_rpcsec_gss.c:918-1156), read in full. Reviewers: round 1 (CLIENT_STALE claimed for no matching server name) right: that path only returns FALSE (1018-1023); round 15 (the lock is not acquired on the svc_getargs failure path) right: the failure return at 957-958 precedes the sx_xlock at 965. The old text said the lock is held on every path; it is held only around the accept call.

name: xprt_active
prose: Precondition: xprt->xp_group and xprt->xp_pool are valid. Postcondition: returns nothing. It takes grp->sg_lock and releases it before returning. If xp_registered is FALSE it returns without changing the transport. Otherwise, only when xp_active was FALSE, it sets xp_active to TRUE and, when xp_thread is NULL, appends xprt to grp->sg_active if request space is not available for the pool, or if xprt_assignthread finds no idle thread; xprt_assignthread, when an idle thread exists, removes it from the idle list, takes a reference on xprt, sets xp_thread and the thread's transport and signals the thread, and when none exists may set grp->sg_state to SVCPOOL_THREADWANTED (if the group is ACTIVE, the last thread creation was before the current time and the thread count is below the maximum). A transport that already has xp_active TRUE, or a non-NULL xp_thread, is otherwise left unchanged.
note: Slice cut the head; real function xprt_active (svc.c:433-458), with xprt_assignthread (400-430), read in full. Reviewers right: round 1 (a non-NULL xp_thread skips assign/append, 449) and round 15 (xprt_assignthread may set SVCPOOL_THREADWANTED, 423-427). The request-space check at 450 skips the assign attempt entirely and appends.

name: smist_set
prose: Precondition: dev has a smist softc whose two settings sets[0] and sets[1] are filled; set->freq should match one of them. Postcondition: returns EINVAL when set->freq matches neither sets[0].freq nor sets[1].freq (CPUFREQ_CMP). Otherwise it calls getset_state with GET_STATE and ignores the return value; getset_state writes the reported state (low bit of the value returned by the SMI) into its state argument before it checks for errors, so state is set even when it returns ENXIO, but its input value, which is passed to the SMI, is an uninitialized int in this function. If that state equals the requested state it returns 0. Otherwise it calls getset_state with SET_STATE up to three times, delaying 200 microseconds after each failure; because getset_state stores the reported state into its argument, req_state itself is overwritten by each SET_STATE call before the next retry. It returns 0 as soon as getset_state returns 0, or the last nonzero value (ENXIO, or EINVAL for a bad function) after three failures.
note: Read smist.c:233-275 and 447-479. Reviewers right: round 1 (a GET_STATE SMI is done before returning 0 and its error is ignored, 463-465), round 15 (the state is set before getset_state returns an error: line 262 *state = new_state & 1 precedes the switch at 264). Not covered by either reviewer: the call passes uninitialized state as the SMI input and overwrites req_state on retries.

name: smist_type
prose: Precondition: dev is the device and type is a pointer that may be NULL. Postcondition: returns EINVAL without writing when type is NULL; otherwise it stores CPUFREQ_TYPE_ABSOLUTE through type and returns 0. It takes no locks.
note: Slice has no head: real function smist_type (smist.c:507-515), read in full (store at 513).

name: msix_release
prose: Precondition: irq is an interrupt source number; the caller does not hold msi_lock (the function takes it). Postcondition: it takes msi_lock, looks up the source for irq and returns ENOENT (lock released) if there is none, or EINVAL (lock released) if the source is not an MSI-X message. Otherwise (the message must be owned, asserted with KASSERT) it, in an IOMMU build, drops msi_lock around iommu_unmap_msi_intr(msi_dev, msi_remap_cookie) and takes it again, then clears msi_first, msi_dev, calls apic_free_vector for the message's cpu, vector and irq, clears msi_vector, msi_msix, msi_count and msi_maxcount, releases msi_lock and returns 0.
note: Slice cut the head: real function msix_release (msi.c:760-795), read in full. The old prose said the function always returns 0 and that the caller holds msi_lock; both wrong: ENOENT/EINVAL returns exist (766-775) and the function acquires the lock itself.

name: set_percpu_callback
prose: Precondition: vcpu is any unsigned int; it is stored unchanged into the vcpu field of the hypercall argument structure. Postcondition: it issues HYPERVISOR_hvm_op(HVMOP_set_evtchn_upcall_vector) with vector IDT_EVTCHN for that vcpu and returns 0 when the hypercall returns 0, otherwise the value returned by xen_translate_error applied to the hypercall's error value (what range that function returns was not read here). It holds no locks and keeps no references.
note: Slice cut the head; real function set_percpu_callback (hvm.c:312-322), read in full. Reviewer round 1 (vcpu <= 255 precondition wrong) right: vcpu is stored in a full field (317). Contract left empty because it called an external translation function. The previous text asserted the translated value is a positive errno: not verified.

name: xenbusb_write_ivar
prose: Precondition: child is a xenbus device child with valid ivars. Postcondition: for XENBUS_IVAR_STATE it takes ivars->xd_lock exclusively and releases it before returning. If xd_state already equals the requested state it returns 0 with no xenstore access. Otherwise it runs a xenstore transaction that reads the node's "state" entry and rewrites it (retrying on EAGAIN, restarting the transaction while xs_transaction_end reports failure). Any error aborts the transaction (xs_transaction_end with abort when error is nonzero, after logging a fatal device error for a write failure unless the new state is Closing); in that case xd_state is not changed. On a committed transaction it sets xd_state, and if XDF_CONNECTING is set and the new state is Closed or Connected it clears that flag and releases the config hook, then wakes sleepers on xd_state. The result for the STATE case is the error, except that ENOENT is converted to 0 (so that return can happen with xd_state not updated). XENBUS_IVAR_NODE, TYPE, OTHEREND_ID and OTHEREND_PATH return EINVAL (read-only); any other index returns ENOENT.
note: Slice cut the head; real function xenbusb_write_ivar (xenbusb.c:897-983), read in full. Reviewers right: round 1 (ENOENT returns 0 without updating xd_state, 969), round 15 (config hook release also requires XDF_CONNECTING set, 946).

name: ATF_TC_BODY(aio_socket_two_reads, tc)
prose: Generated function aio_socket_two_reads_body(tc), produced by ATF_TC_BODY(aio_socket_two_reads, tc). It takes the ATF test case pointer and returns void; it requires the "aio" kernel module (ATF_REQUIRE_KERNEL_MODULE) and, only when compiled with __FreeBSD_version below 1100101, contains a skip call (spelled aft_tc_skip in the source, so that old-kernel case is a compile-time branch, not a run-time check). It creates a PF_UNIX SOCK_STREAM socketpair, queues two aio_read requests on s[0] (each must return 0), writes one byte (0xc3) to s[1], requires aio_waitcomplete to return 1, finds which of the two requests completed and requires its buffer[0] to equal the byte, requires the other request to report EINPROGRESS from aio_error and aio_cancel(s[0], that request) to return AIO_CANCELED, and closes both sockets. A failing ATF_REQUIRE terminates the test case at that point (the sockets are then not closed by this function).
note: Read aio_test.c:1125-1178. The prior text matched except that the old-kernel skip is a compile-time #if branch with a misspelled call aft_tc_skip (1138-1141), and the precondition is established inside the function, not by the caller (reviewer round 1 on preconditions right).
